data_fields.name: victim_rule
data_fields.donor_constant: lowest playing priority, kicked only if strictly below the new sound's priority; atmos priority 0x7FFFFFFE

data_fields.name: stack_limit_max
data_fields.donor_constant: N from STACK=limit:N, minimum 1; no policy = one start per sample per audio tick

data_fields.name: duck_gain_rule
data_fields.donor_constant: gain = base / sqrt(active count); max 0 = uncapped

data_fields.name: atmos_chance_one_in
data_fields.donor_constant: 800 (MEDIUM); LOW 3200; HIGH 400; drawn once per update call

data_fields.name: atmos_bed_modulo
data_fields.donor_constant: k % 40 == 0 (about 1 in 40 of the non-one-shot draws)

data_fields.name: room_bed_search_cells
data_fields.donor_constant: 11 x 11 = 121 slabs around the camera, first owned room with a bed wins

best_idea: Keep one fixed voice pool where a new sound kicks the lowest-priority voice only after it has actually started, and cap repeats of one sample with an explicit limit or duck policy.
decision_why: The donor is the only one read with a real per-sample concurrency rule (limit and duck with 1/sqrt(n)) and a priority kick; a many-on-one fight needs both. Adapt because the donor kicks before starting (D1), uses per-call atmos rolls (D2) and hard-cuts beds and music (D3); those are fixed in the sketch.
acceptance: In a three-attacker fight with all 16 voices busy on priority-1 hit cues, a priority-5 finisher plays and exactly one priority-1 voice stops; a priority-1 cue with the pool saturated is refused and stops nothing; a failed backend start stops no voice (unit test).
